subject: Throughput sizing — FinEx follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Lopez <anna.lopez@finexcap.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-10T14:40:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap & next steps — throughput sizing

Hi Anna,

Great to speak earlier. Quick recap from our discovery and the sizing items Rafael and I will need to recommend a target Dedicated configuration and SLA: 

- Target latency SLO: you mentioned 95th <= 300ms for first token (interactive) — please confirm if this is required for all routes or just the UI flows.
- Typical / average QPS: you estimated ~15 qps steady, with peaks up to ~120 qps for scheduled batch runs — confirm.
- Average tokens per request: ~450 tokens (prompt + expected generation). Peak requests could be larger (up to ~2,000 tokens) for some reconciliation jobs.
- Concurrent sessions: you called out ~80 concurrent interactive users during peak, plus background batch jobs.
- Streaming requirements: UI needs streaming first-token within 150ms and token-level streaming for progressive output.

Attached is our initial throughput calc (redwood_throughput_calc_v1.pdf) — it includes a simple tokens/sec and GPU fleet sizing model based on the numbers above. Could you attach the workload profile you referenced (session distribution, percentiles, hourly pattern)? That will let us refine burst capacity and autoscale config.

Next steps: Rafael will propose a preliminary sizing + recommended model variant/quantization options by EOD today. Marissa will follow up with cost delta between steady-state and peak-burst options.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_throughput_calc_v1.pdf (PDF, 180KB)

From: Anna Lopez <anna.lopez@finexcap.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.ai>, procurement@finexcap.com
Date: 2026-07-10T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps — throughput sizing

Thanks Marissa — good recap. I attached the FinEx workload profile (finex_workload_profile.xlsx). A few clarifications inline: 

- Latency: 95th <= 300ms applies to customer-facing UI only. Backend reconciliation jobs can tolerate higher latency (up to 2s).
- QPS: steady-state for UI is closer to 12 qps, not 15. Peak UI bursts (external events) can hit ~90 qps for ~10 minutes. The 120 qps number is for our nightly batch ingestion window (non-interactive).
- Tokens: average 420 tokens per UI request; median is ~300. Batch jobs vary widely, peak single requests up to 4,000 tokens.
- Concurrency: interactive peak active users ~75; we also run ~40 parallel batch workers during ingestion windows.
- Streaming: we need partial token streaming for UI flows (first token under 150ms, subsequent tokens at ~30-50ms/token).

Let us know if you need distribution histograms for request sizes or per-route breakdowns — I can ask the infra team to export.

Anna Lopez
Head of ML Infrastructure
FinEx Capital

Attachments: finex_workload_profile.xlsx (XLSX, 85KB)

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Anna Lopez <anna.lopez@finexcap.com>
Date: 2026-07-10T18:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps — throughput sizing

Thanks Anna — the clarifications help. Quick technical follow-up / rough calc based on the numbers provided: 

Assumptions used: UI avg tokens = 420, steady UI QPS = 12, peak UI QPS = 90 (10 min bursts), batch peak QPS (ingest) = 120 but non-streaming and tolerant latency. Model: gpt-open-16k-ish quantized baseline for cost/latency estimates.

- Steady-state tokens/sec (UI): 12 qps * 420 tokens = 5,040 tokens/sec.
- Peak UI tokens/sec: 90 qps * 420 = 37,800 tokens/sec.
- Peak batch tokens/sec (worst-case single-window): 120 qps * 2,000 tokens (conservative) = 240,000 tokens/sec for a short window — this likely needs batching & backpressure.

GPU sizing notes (very rough):
- For interactive SLOs (95p <= 300ms, streaming first token <=150ms), we'd target low-latency instances with higher per-GPU qps (e.g., provisioned instances with optimized kernels). A small dedicated pool of 2-4 GPUs could cover steady-state at reduced concurrency with autoscale to handle 10-min bursts (policy-based warm pools).
- For the ingest batch window, we recommend a separate batch fleet or scheduled capacity reservation because of the tokens/sec magnitude. Alternatively, use rate-limited ingestion to smooth the burst.

Questions for FinEx: 
1) Can batch jobs be scheduled to avoid overlapping with peak interactive windows?
2) Do you prefer a single mixed pool (serve both interactive + batch) or separate dedicated fleets (simplicity vs cost)?
3) Can you provide the percentile histogram for request sizes (p50/p90/p99) per route?

I'll convert the rough calc into a sizing proposal with recommended GPU counts, autoscale triggers, and cost estimates tomorrow morning.

-Rafael
Engineering Lead, Performance
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Lopez <anna.lopez@finexcap.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.ai>, procurement@finexcap.com
Date: 2026-07-11T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps — throughput sizing

Anna — thanks for the fast turnaround and the attachment. Summarizing next steps so we have alignment: 

- Rafael will deliver a formal sizing proposal (GPU counts, recommended model variant, quantization options, autoscale policies, and cost delta steady vs peak) — ETA: 2026-07-11 11:30 PT.
- FinEx to confirm whether batch windows can be shifted or smoothed; if yes, we model a single pool with autoscale; if not, we model a separate batch fleet.
- Marissa will prepare an internal estimate for reserved capacity pricing (Dedicated) and a short comparison vs hosted burstable option — ETA: EOD 2026-07-11.
- Procurement (cc) — please share any procurement timelines or PO templates we should factor in.

If you can share the p50/p90/p99 request-size histograms, Rafael can tighten the GPU count and autoscale thresholds.

Talk soon — appreciate the quick responses.

Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: redwood_throughput_calc_v1.pdf, finex_workload_profile.xlsx
